title: Organise and coordinate the implementation of the weekly production plan to achieve young plant production targets of the nursery

lessons.title: Understanding the weekly production plan
lessons.html:
From the manager's plan to your week

Young plant production is the engine of the nursery. Seedlings, plugs, rooted cuttings and liners produced this week become the finished plants sold months later. If this week's targets are missed, the gap shows up later as empty benches and unfilled orders.

What is in a weekly production plan

The manager usually gives the supervisor a weekly plan that lists:

  • Which plants and varieties to sow, stick or transplant.
  • How many trays, plugs or cuttings for each.
  • Which day each task is due.
  • The materials needed: seed, cutting material, trays, media, rooting hormone, labels.
  • Where the batches must go: mist house, germination room, tunnel or shade house.

Example plan extract

DayTaskTarget
MondaySow petunia plug trays120 trays
TuesdayStick lavender cuttings4 000 cuttings
WednesdayTransplant marigold plugs300 trays
ThursdayStick plumbago cuttings3 000 cuttings
FridayWean tissue-culture plantlets1 500 plants

Check the plan before the week starts

Read the plan by Thursday or Friday of the week before. Ask yourself: Do I have enough workers? Is the seed and cutting material available and healthy? Is there space in the mist house? Are trays and media in stock? Is any equipment due for repair? Raise problems with the manager early, while there is still time to fix them, rather than discovering them on Monday morning.

Understanding why each target exists also helps. If the 4 000 lavender cuttings are for a big retail order in spring, you know that the task cannot slip.

lessons.title: Organising people, materials and space
lessons.html:
Getting ready to deliver the targets

Work out the labour needed

Use known work rates to calculate how many people you need. For example, if one experienced worker sticks about 1 000 cuttings a day in your nursery, and the target is 4 000, you need about four experienced workers for the day, or more if some are still learning. Use your own nursery's records for work rates; do not guess.

Allocate the right people

Match workers to tasks. Put your fastest, most careful workers on difficult tasks such as tissue-culture weaning or grafting, and pair new workers with experienced ones. Keep a skills list of who is trained on which task.

Prepare materials in advance

  • Have seed counted and checked against the plan the day before sowing.
  • Arrange for cutting material to be collected early in the morning when stock plants are cool and full of water.
  • Fill and label trays ahead of time if possible.
  • Mix rooting hormone and other inputs exactly as the label instructs, wearing the required protective equipment.

Prepare space

Clean and disinfect benches before new batches go in. Check that the mist system, bottom heat and lights are working. Plan where each batch will sit so that batches can be moved on at the right time without blocking each other.

Communicate the plan

Explain the week's targets in the Monday morning meeting. Write the daily targets on a board in the propagation area so that everyone knows what success looks like each day.

Safety

Propagation areas are humid and floors may be wet and slippery. Keep paths clear, report electrical faults on mist and heating systems immediately and never let untrained workers repair them.

lessons.title: Monitoring progress and adjusting the plan
lessons.html:
Keeping the week on track

Check progress during each day

Count output at mid-morning, lunch and the end of the day. If the team has stuck 1 500 of the 4 000 cuttings by lunch, you know early that you are behind and can add people or extend the task. Waiting until 16:30 to discover a shortfall leaves no time to act.

Check quality, not only quantity

Fast work is useless if it is poor. Check that:

  • Seed is sown at the right depth and density.
  • Cuttings are the correct length, with the right leaves removed and inserted to the right depth.
  • Every tray is labelled with plant name, date and batch number.
  • Plugs are transplanted without damaging roots.
  • Hygiene rules are followed.

Record the results

At the end of each day record what was done against the target, any losses, and the reasons for any shortfall. Later, record germination and strike rates for each batch. These records show the manager whether the young plant targets will be met and help to improve future plans.

Dealing with problems

Common problems include late seed, poor cutting material, absent workers, breakdowns and hot weather. Solve what you can, for example by moving workers from a less urgent task, and report anything that will affect the week's targets to the manager straight away, with a suggested solution. Never change plant varieties or quantities without approval.

Weekly review

At the end of the week compare total output with the plan, list what went well and what went wrong, and agree on improvements for the next week with the manager and the team.

Key points

  • Read the weekly plan early and raise resource problems before the week starts.
  • Use known work rates to calculate the labour needed.
  • Prepare materials, space and equipment in advance.
  • Check quantity and quality several times a day.
  • Record output, losses and reasons, and report shortfalls early.

quiz.question: When should a supervisor read the weekly production plan?

options.text: On Friday afternoon of the same week
Only when the manager asks about progress
Before the week starts, so problems can be raised early

quiz.question: A worker sticks about 1 000 cuttings a day and the target is 4 000. About how many experienced workers are needed for one day?
When is the best time to collect cutting material from stock plants?

options.text: In the heat of the afternoon
Early in the morning when plants are cool and full of water

quiz.question: Why count output at mid-morning and lunch?

options.text: To find out early if the team is behind and act
To give workers a longer break
Because the plan says nothing about targets

quiz.question: What should you do if poor cutting material will make you miss a target?

options.text: Change the plant variety without telling anyone
Hide the shortfall in the records
Use the cuttings anyway and say nothing
Report it to the manager straight away with a suggested solution

quiz.question: Fast work is acceptable even if cuttings are inserted at the wrong depth.
Benches should be cleaned and disinfected before new batches go in.
